main_body: A flat seamless ground patch of green grass tiles (named 'desert' but drawn in green), repeating tufts on a uniform mid-green base; no standing volume.
top_band: none - terrain tile viewed flat; the column scan only shows repeating grass tuft marks (L=85/111/139), no top band over a front face
evidence: Terrain ground patch, not a standing object, so the 3/4 top+front contract does not apply. It has no walls, cliffs or raised volume that would need a top band or front face, and no side face is drawn. Passes as terrain.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours and a median of 4 colours per tile, against 80 colours and 26 per tile for the reference grass. The ground is a single flat mid-green with only three tone steps (dark, mid, light) in sparse repeated tuft stamps. The tufts repeat identically every 16px in a visible grid, which looks stamped. Flat-fill coverage is 14% versus 0% for the grass reference. There is no soil grain, speckle or clump variation, and it reads as much thinner and flatter than the Beodeul grass. The 0% neutral edge share only shows that nothing is outlined. The name 'desert' also does not match green grass, though hue is not judged.
